subject: Dataflow authorization request for logging partner - Nimbus Observability
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>; Alice Chen <alice@nimbus-observability.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: authorization to engage Nimbus Observability for application logs

Hi team / Alice,

We're evaluating Nimbus Observability to replace our current logging forwarder for Redwood's hosted inference clusters. Short summary: Nimbus will receive aggregated application logs (structured JSON), traces, and optional error payloads from hosted API nodes. They would store indices in both eu-west-1 and us-west-2 and offer a separate customer-controlled retention window.

Why I'm flagging this: some log fields may contain token IDs and minimally redacted user identifiers. Legal asked we treat this as a subprocessor change and confirm onward-transfer permissions (DPA / SCCs) before we flip the switch.

Ask: can you review and advise on the minimum evidence we need to approve them for production? Items I expect we'll need: SOC 2 report, list of subprocessors, confirmation of data locations, retention controls, and whether they can sign SCCs / a BAA if needed. I'm attaching our DPIA template and a draft dataflow diagram they asked for.

If procurement/legal are comfortable we can run a 30-day staging ingest in eu-west-1. Timeline request from product is tight: they'd like a decision by Oct 15 so the pilot can start Oct 20.

Thanks,
Hannah
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPIA_template.docx, dataflow-diagram.drawio

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>; Alice Chen <alice@nimbus-observability.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: authorization to engage Nimbus Observability for application logs

Hannah — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the DPIA draft. Quick legal checklist so procurement knows what's non-negotiable before we allow any production ingest: 

- Current SOC 2 Type II report (prefer last 12 months) or SOC 3 if SOC2 is unavailable, plus scope (does it include logging pipeline?).
- Full subprocessor roster and any planned onward transfers (need names + locations).
- Confirmed DPA template (we will ask for SCCs if data is EU-origin and vendor does not offer adequate adequacy).
- Encryption at rest and in transit details, KMS options, and access controls for Redwood data.
- Data retention default and ability to set customer-specific retention windows; deletion/erasure process.
- DPIA trigger assessment: because logs may contain identifiers and token IDs, we likely need a DPIA completed and signed off by privacy. I attached the company DPIA template; please ask vendor to fill sections on processing purposes, categories of data, risk mitigations, and subprocessors.

Procurement: please add Nimbus to the vendor registry as "pending evidence". We should not send live production logs to any vendor flagged as pending. Staging is fine if it's synthetic or scrubbed.

CC: Markus — can you verify whether our infra team can run an isolated, scrubbed-forwarding workflow for the Oct pilot?

Monica
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: DPIA_template.docx

From: Alice Chen <alice@nimbus-observability.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@nimbus-observability.com
Date: 2026-10-12T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: authorization to engage Nimbus Observability for application logs

Hi Hannah / Monica / team,

Thanks for the detailed note — we appreciate the checklist. Attached are the items you asked for: Nimbus_SOC2_Report_2026Q2.pdf and our current nimbus-subprocessors-roster.csv. High-level responses below:

- SOC 2 Type II: attached (audit period Apr 2025–Mar 2026); scope includes our ingestion and storage subsystems.
- Subprocessors: roster includes our CDN, hosted object store (eu & us regions), and a managed key provider. All subprocessors are subject to our standard DPA.
- Data locations: we can pin customer data to eu-west-1 only for the pilot; otherwise we replicate for failover to us-west-2.
- Retention: default 90 days, configurable down to 7 days; retention/deletion APIs available.
- Encryption: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest; customer can bring their own key via supported KMS providers.
- SCCs / DPA: we have a standard DPA and accept SCCs; I've included a DocuSign prepare link for our DPA so you can review and execute.

Regarding the DPIA: happy to complete the vendor sections of your template. I attached a filled vendor section in the Drive link and the subprocessors roster CSV. If you need additional clarifications on whether our processing allows re-identification, I can have our privacy engineer provide a short note.

Let us know whether you want us to proceed with the DocuSign DPA or if legal prefers redlines first. We can also provide a limited-time staging token and a scrubber rule set for the Oct pilot.

Regards,
Alice Chen
Head of Partnerships | Nimbus Observability

Attachments: Nimbus_SOC2_Report_2026Q2.pdf, nimbus-subprocessors-roster.csv
Links: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/DPA-Nimbus-Redwood

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@nimbus-observability.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: authorization to engage Nimbus Observability for application logs

Alice / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Legal, procurement, and infra have reviewed the SOC2 and the subprocessors CSV. Action items and decision: 

1) Procurement will initiate the DPA execution via DocuSign. Monica — if you want redlines, please attach them by COB Nov 9; otherwise procurement will execute the standard DPA.
2) Infra (Markus) confirmed we can run a scrubbed staging stream to eu-west-1 the week of Nov 8 for validation. Markus, please confirm the scrub rules list is acceptable.
3) Privacy asked Nimbus to complete section 3–5 of our DPIA template; Alice indicated the vendor sections are available in the Drive. Please upload the completed vendor DPIA to the shared drive once done.

Assuming we get the DPA executed and the DPIA vendor sections uploaded, this thread can be closed and we will move to a 30-day pilot. Hannah: please add an entry to the vendor registry with status "DPA pending / pilot scheduled" and include the pilot start date once confirmed.

Thanks — moving to procurement execution.

Sergio
Senior Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: dataflow-diagram.drawio
